title: Autoscale strategy compiler for tokenized QoS contracts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a policy compiler that converts high-level tenant QoS contracts (tokenized throughput SLAs, p95 latency ceilings, and availability buckets) into concrete autoscaling graphs that the Dedicated Fleet controller can execute. The compiler will accept a compact declarative contract language (examples below) and produce: 1) target metric bindings (tokens/sec per slot, queue-depth thresholds, latency-percentile monitors), 2) scaling algorithm instantiation (PID/PI, rate-limited stepper, predictive warm-up with headroom credits), and 3) safety envelope primitives (max surge capacity, eviction window, cooldown policies, rollback policies). The goal is to let product/solutions engineers specify per-tenant QoS in business terms while ensuring generated policies are bounded by fleet-wide safety constraints and cost/latency tradeoffs.
acceptance_criteria: Compiler accepts declarative contract examples and produces a validated policy graph JSON that conforms to the autoscaler runtime schema
Generated policy graphs include explicit metric bindings for: tokens_per_second, p95_latency_ms, queue_depth, and active_connections
Safety primitives are injected by default: max_surge_percent, min_instances, cooldown_seconds, and eviction_priority_rules
End-to-end test: submit a contract in staging and observe the Dedicated controller enact scaling decisions in the simulator without exceeding surge caps
Integration tests for rollback path: when a model variant degrades quality metrics, compiler-generated fallback policies trigger and scale down gracefully per configured cooldown
notes: We intentionally separate semantic contract from execution graph to keep the language stable as runtime evolves
Tradeoff: stronger default safety limits reduce potential SLA fulfillment for bursty enterprise tenants; include opt-in override flag for committed contracts under legal review
Consider using quantile-targeter as first-class primitive to map p95 latency targets into headroom credits
Compiler should emit instrumentation hooks for Console observability (route->policy mapping, applied headroom, decision timestamps)
Will coordinate with Runtime team to ensure schema fields are compatible with runtime-1.21 and planned dedicated-2026.04 release
tasks: Draft minimal DSL and example contracts
Implement parser and AST -> policy-graph emitter
Add safety injection pass with fleet-level guardrails
Unit tests for metric binding and scaling algorithm selection
Run simulator scenarios for 10 tenant profiles and capture overshoot/undershoot metrics
Wire emitted policy graph into the Dedicated controller test harness
Add Console mapping and telemetry events for policy decisions
